parties.counterparty: SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor)

plans.note: Liability language in this form typically sits with or immediately after the all-caps warranty disclaimer block (Article VIX and the p0109/p0112/p0116 run-on headings); check for a consequential-damages exclusion and any cap, whether it is mutual, and whether confidentiality, IP infringement and willful misconduct are carved out. Sweep General Provisions as a fallback location.

No indemnity heading appears in the outline; a licensor IP indemnity, if present, would likely be tucked into the licence restrictions (Article II), the warranty/disclaimer article, or General Provisions. Also check for a one-way Licensee indemnity running to SFG, which would be a direction problem. Confirm absence across the full text before treating as missing.

Field-of-use and licence restrictions in Article II are the most likely source of any restraint on our business; the Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation article (X / p0123) often carries a bolted-on non-compete. Also test the 'Right of First Refusal' defined term, which can operate as a de facto restraint on building or buying competing platforms.

'Right of First Refusal' and 'FIELD OF USE' are defined in Article I, so the operative exclusivity or ROFR mechanic should sit in Article II or Article VIII; verify whether we are barred from sourcing competing FX platform services or must offer SFG first refusal on future work.

The tiered per-ticket price table (p0059–p0063) and the Supplemental Payments definition are where any most-favoured-customer language would appear. Likely no MFN at all; only flag if we are obliged to extend SFG our best terms — an MFN running in our favour is welcome and should be left alone.

Article X is expressly headed 'CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION'. Check duration, whether it binds only Licensee or is mutual, whether it reaches employees/contractors/customers, and whether general advertising and unsolicited applicants are carved out.

No article is captioned Term/Termination in the outline; the 'Initial Period' definition in Article I points to term mechanics likely in Article VIII, with wind-down possibly in Article XXIV/General Provisions. Look for whether we may exit on notice without penalty and whether SFG can terminate at will mid-term or on our non-payment of Supplemental Payments.

Trace the 'Initial Period' defined term from Article I to the renewal mechanic (likely Article VIII). Assess notice window for non-renewal, automatic rollover length, and any uncapped price uplift on renewal; a missing uplift cap is a rationale note, not a standalone deviation.

Governing law, venue and any dispute-resolution or arbitration clause will sit in the General Provisions block (Article XXIV / p0144). New York is expected given the 575 Madison Avenue addresses and would be compliant; flag only foreign law or offshore arbitration.

Assignment/successors-and-assigns language belongs in General Provisions. Confirm we may assign to AFFILIATEs (defined in Article I) and to a successor by merger or asset sale, and that SFG has no termination right triggered by our change of control.

Article I defines DERIVATIVE WORK, INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS, MORAL RIGHTS, LICENSED TECHNOLOGY and PLATFORM SOFTWARE; Article II carries the grant and restrictions. Check for any assignment to Licensor of our data, feedback, configurations or derivative works — Licensor retaining its own pre-existing platform IP is expected and should not be flagged.

Article II is the grant clause. Test scope against FIELD OF USE and AFFILIATE definitions: whether affiliates and our contractors/introducing brokers may use the Platform, and whether the grant is revocable at Licensor's discretion rather than only on uncured breach.

Any usage-verification or books-and-records inspection right would sit with the licence restrictions (Article II) or with the per-ticket volume/pricing and Supplemental Payments mechanics in Article VIII. Check frequency, notice, on-site scope and who bears cost before concluding it is absent.

Look in the fee/volume article for penalty interest, shortfall charges or stipulated damages payable by us on early termination or missed volumes. Service credits or remedies flowing to us are beneficial and must not be flagged.

Article VIX contains an all-caps WARRANTY DISCLAIMER expressly negating merchantability, non-infringement and fitness for purpose and disclaiming that errors will be corrected — assess whether any affirmative performance warranty survives it and whether a repair/replace or refund remedy exists; this looks like a likely deviation rather than a mere note.

No insurance heading appears in the outline; if present it would be in General Provisions. Given SFG hosts the Platform and handles our trade data, confirm across the full text before recording as missing.

The tiered per-ticket pricing table (0-10 through 50+) plus the 'Supplemental Payments' and 'Market Day' definitions strongly suggest volume-based economics; check for a minimum monthly/annual ticket commitment, true-up or take-or-pay and whether an exit exists. Volume discounts alone are not a commitment.

Look for post-termination obligations near the licence restrictions (return/destruction of LICENSED SOFTWARE and DOCUMENTATION) and in Article X/General Provisions for return of Confidential Information. Note that return of our materials to us, as distinct from our return of Licensor property, appears unaddressed; confirm before marking missing.
